query: We're about to turn on Agentic Commerce Search for our site. Before we do, capture what the storefront search page shows for our top 30 queries so we have a native baseline.
Agentic Commerce Search was switched on yesterday. Capture the storefront search results again with the same settings and compare them with the baseline we took before.
Does the search page on our dev storefront show the same products as the Shopper Search API for 'red dress' and 'running shoes'? I think a customization changes the order.
I turned on Agentic Commerce Search but the storefront search results look the same as before. How can I tell whether the page is really being served by the new engine?
Capture the storefront search pages with the price low to high sort and a color filter applied, using the same queries as last time.
Our staging storefront is behind the storefront password. How do I capture its search results pages from the CLI without putting the password in my shell history?
Run the full four-way comparison: storefront and API, before and after Agentic Commerce Search is on, and summarize the findings for me.
The storefront capture warns that no product tiles were found. How do I save the HTML and fix the selectors for our customized search template?
Agentic Commerce Search is already live on our site and I forgot to take a baseline. Is there any way to still get the storefront's native search results?
Why don't the product IDs from the storefront search page match the master product IDs the Shopper Search API returns for the same query?
Compare lexical and semantic search results from the Shopper Search API for our top queries and show me the overlap at the top 1, 5, and 10 results.
Capture the Shopper Search API results for the queries in queries.txt in semantic mode, sorted by price, and check that the sort was applied.
Create a SLAS client for guest shoppers with the shopper product search scope.
Our storefront search page is slow at peak traffic. Which Metrics API signals should I look at to find where the time goes?
Purge the CDN cache for the storefront search pages so shoppers see the new content.
